name: Speech Impediment, Stuttering, or Mechanical Conditions (from surgery or trauma)
name_in_guide: SPEECH IMPEDIMENT, STUTTERING, OR MECHANICAL CONDITIONS (from surgery or trauma)

category.name: Mouth and Throat
category.part: AME Physical Examination Information and Disposition Tables

what_to_bring: Effective communication with air traffic control; and
A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with a speech-language pathologist no more than 90 days before the AME exam. It must include:
Detailed summary of the history of the condition;
Current medications, dosage, and side effects (if any);
It must specifically include the cause for stuttering and the intelligible their speech is.
Speech Fluency/Intelligibility test for those with mechanical problems;
Any testing deemed necessary or already performed by the treating provider.

rows.label: A
rows.condition: Resolved OR Does not impair voice communication.
rows.evaluation_data: If the AME can determine the condition has resolved without sequelae with no symptoms or current problems that would interfere with flight duties: - Communication needed for flight (emergency procedures; - Effective communication with air traffic control; and - Crew-cockpit communication).
rows.evaluation_data_html:
If the AME can determine the condition has resolved without sequelae with no symptoms or current problems that would interfere with flight duties:

  • Communication needed for flight (emergency procedures;
  • Effective communication with air traffic control; and
  • Crew-cockpit communication).
what_to_bring: Effective communication with air traffic control; and
rows.disposition: ISSUE Annotate this information in Block 60.

rows.label: B
rows.condition: Condition, including stuttering, that would impair voice communication
rows.condition_html:
B.

Condition, including stuttering, that would impair voice communication
rows.evaluation_data: Submit the following for FAA review: - 1. A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with a speech-language pathologist no more than 90 days before the AME exam. It must include: - Detailed summary of the history of the condition; - Current medications, dosage, and side effects (if any); - Physical exam findings; - Results of any testing performed; - Diagnosis; - Assessment; - Plan (prognosis); and - Follow-up. - 2. It must specifically include the cause for stuttering and the intelligible their speech is. - Stuttering Severity Index for those who stutter; - Speech Fluency/Intelligibility test for those with mechanical problems; - 3. Any testing deemed necessary or already performed by the treating provider. The speech-language pathologist or AME should describe any functional limitations that could affect the pilot's ability to operate aircraft controls or communicate with other pilots or ATCS.
rows.evaluation_data_html:
Submit the following for FAA review:

  • 1. A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with a speech-language pathologist no more than 90 days before the AME exam. It must include:
  • Detailed summary of the history of the condition;
  • Current medications, dosage, and side effects (if any);
  • Physical exam findings;
  • Results of any testing performed;
  • Diagnosis;
  • Assessment;
  • Plan (prognosis); and
  • Follow-up.
  • 2. It must specifically include the cause for stuttering and the intelligible their speech is.
    • Stuttering Severity Index for those who stutter;
    • Speech Fluency/Intelligibility test for those with mechanical problems;
  • 3. Any testing deemed necessary or already performed by the treating provider.

The speech-language pathologist or AME should describe any functional limitations that could affect the pilot's ability to operate aircraft controls or communicate with other pilots or ATCS.
